entries.test: Whether, by June 2026, LLM guardrail adequacy had become a prominent political and policy matter, such as the White House making Anthropic's Fable 5 rerelease conditional on jailbreak-proof guardrails.
entries.note: "Central issue" is loose, but the plain reading is that guardrails had become a live government policy fight. The embedded tweet is dated Feb 2024, while he says January 2024.

entries.test: Whether any LLM has guardrails demonstrated to withstand all jailbreak attempts, judged by public red-teaming and jailbreak research.
entries.note: He endorses the security experts' view as reported by WIRED.

entries.test: Whether, as of January 2024, any deployed LLM guardrail avoided both widespread over-refusal and routine jailbreaks, judged by contemporaneous evaluations.
entries.note: He quotes his own January 2024 piece, co-written with Katie Conrad. The proposition leaves out "virtually any guardrail" from the setup, but the core claim is kept.

entries.test: Whether, as of June 2026, any deployed LLM guardrail avoided both significant over-refusal and routine jailbreaks, judged by public safety evaluations and red-teaming.
entries.note: He reaffirms the 2024 claim as of the post date.
The proposition adds a causal link ("which is why their guardrails fail") that the sentence does not state. Readers would not agree on how to test "built for safety".
This is a policy dilemma framed as a choice, not a testable claim.

entries.test: Whether generative AI models from other vendors (OpenAI, Google, Meta, etc.) are also routinely jailbroken, judged by public red-teaming results.
entries.note: Context ties "this" to the inability to block all jailbreaks.
